Spec review companion · #149 · snapshot 892b237 · 2026-10-28

Read no untracked file that git reaches only through a link

Read the open sections in about ten minutes. Everything closed is a look-up. A file:line chip jumps to the source line at the bottom, for when a claim needs checking.

Bug #149

The change

On Windows, a review named every untracked file behind a directory junction, and read the text of one whose real path was in the repo, such as an ignored secrets/ folder. assessment:35

Each path through a link folder now becomes that folder, shown once as skipped, and its Git Status lines are dropped. fix:10

1code file fix:19
10tests that fail on the old code fix:47
6checks, all as expected test:21
4deviations fix:88

Root cause

The untracked list kept every path git printed, and the real-path check of #110 hid only the text. assessment:67

Remediation

Check each folder on a path with lstat; filter Git Status by the same folders. assessment:76

# Bug Assessment: a review names the untracked files behind a folder link, and Copilot can read them - **Slug**: 149-skip-files-through-links- **Created**: 2026-10-28- **Source**: pasted text (issue #149, with a probe of Copilot CLI 1.0.95 made on 2026-10-28)- **Verdict**: valid- **Severity**: medium ## Report (verbatim or summarized) Issue #149, "Read no untracked file that git reaches only through a link". #110 stopped a reviewfrom putting the text of an untracked file whose real path is outside the repo or in a `.git` folderinto the prompt and `untracked.md`. Code review of #110 found three gaps: - Git for Windows walks into an untracked directory junction and lists every file behind it. The  names still reach Git Status, the changed-file list and the untracked headers, and git walks the  whole outside tree, which can be slow.- In self-collect mode Copilot runs in the repo with its own file tools; a junction lets them open  files outside the repo.- A junction to a git-ignored folder inside the repo makes git list its files as untracked. Their  real path is inside the repo and not in `.git`, so their text is read. Expected: a review reads no untracked file that git reaches only through a link, and sends Copilotno names of such files; Copilot's file tools cannot reach a file through a link, or the READMEstates the limit. The probe (Windows, real Copilot CLI 1.0.95, a read-only task, the same tool profile as a review):in a repo with `linkdir` as a junction to an outside folder holding `key.txt`, Copilot's `view` toolopened `linkdir\key.txt` and printed its marker. `glob` (`**/*.txt`) and `grep` did not follow thejunction. A second probe, in a repo with no link: `view` opened `.git/config` and printed a markerset with `git config`. ## Symptom On Windows, a working-tree review names each file behind an untracked junction, in Git Status, theuntracked list and (self-collect) the changed-file list, and reads the text of one whose real path isinside the repo, such as an ignored `secrets/` folder reached through a junction. On every system,Copilot's `view` tool can open a file through a folder link in the repo. Expected: no name or text ofsuch a file reaches Copilot; the link itself is shown once as skipped. ## Reproduction 1. On Windows, in a git repo, make `secrets/` with `key.txt` holding a marker, add `secrets/` to   `.gitignore`, and make `seclink` a junction to `secrets`. Make `linkdir` a junction to a folder   outside the repo with `key.txt`.2. `collectReviewContext` (working tree) gives `### seclink/key.txt` with the marker's text,   `### linkdir/key.txt (skipped: symlink)`, and `?? linkdir/key.txt` and `?? seclink/key.txt` in   Git Status.3. On macOS and Linux, git lists `linkdir` and `seclink` as single untracked entries (a symlink), so   only the Copilot tool gap applies there. ## Suspected Code Paths - `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/git.mjs:156` `getWorkingTreeState`: takes `git ls-files --others`  as is; every caller (the untracked list, the changed-file list, the counts, `writeReviewPatches`)  uses it.- `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/git.mjs:289` `collectWorkingTreeContext`: Git Status is a separate  `git status --short --untracked-files=all`.- `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/git.mjs:251` `formatUntrackedFile`: skips the text of a file whose  real path is outside the repo or in `.git`, but keeps its name, and reads one whose real path is  inside (the ignored-folder case).- `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/copilot.mjs` `READ_ONLY_TOOLS`: `view`, `glob`, `grep`; Copilot CLI  checks a path as written, so `view` follows a junction. ## Root Cause Hypothesis The untracked list keeps every path git prints, and Git for Windows walks into a junction because ittreats it as a folder. The real-path check of #110 runs per file and only for the text, so the namestays, and a link to an ignored folder inside the repo passes it. Copilot CLI's own path check usesthe path as written. Confidence: high (the code and the probe). ## Proposed Remediation **Preferred**: - In `getWorkingTreeState`, for each untracked path (git prints it relative to the repo root, the  `cwd` that `collectReviewContext` and `writeReviewPatches` pass), `lstat` each folder on it, from  the top: every part but the last, and for an entry that ends in `/` (git prints a nested repo as  `nested/`) every part. When one is a symbolic link or a junction (Node's `isSymbolicLink()` is  true for both), replace the path with that folder's path, once. So `linkdir/key.txt` and  `linkdir/sub/x.txt` become one entry `linkdir`, which `formatUntrackedFile` already shows as  `(skipped: symlink)`, as on macOS and Linux. A folder that cannot be checked counts as a link.  An entry with no link on it stays as it is, `nested/` too. The answer for each folder is kept for  the call, so a folder is checked once however many files lie behind it. `resolveReviewTarget` may  pass a subfolder; git then prints paths relative to it and a link above it is not seen, but that  caller uses only `isDirty`, which the filter does not change. `getWorkingTreeState` also returns  the link folders it found, as `linkFolders`.- In `collectWorkingTreeContext`, Git Status stays the one `git status --short  --untracked-files=all` call; `dropLinkedStatusLines(status, linkFolders)` (exported from  `git.mjs` for its test) drops each `?? ` line whose name starts with `<link folder>/`, so also a  file that appears behind the link between the two git calls. A name that git put in double  quotes is read back first, by `unquoteGitPath` (exported too). It never throws: an unknown escape  keeps its character, a missing closing quote takes the rest of the line, and bytes that are not  UTF-8 become U+FFFD, so a broken line is still dropped when its start is under a link and kept  otherwise. git writes `\a \b \t \n \v \f \r \" \\` and  `\ooo` (octal bytes of the UTF-8 name) inside the quotes, and quotes a name with a space too  (checked on 2026-10-28: `?? "a b.txt"`). Reading git's quotes back, not predicting them, keeps  the match whichever names a git version quotes. Real links collapse only on Windows, but a folder  that cannot be checked collapses on every system. Tracked lines  are not touched, so a tracked change under a junction stays, and no git call or argument is  added. The `?? <link>` line is then missing from Git Status on Windows; the Untracked Files section  shows the link.- `formatUntrackedFile` keeps its real-path check as a second guard.- Copilot's `view` tool: the plugin cannot limit it (Copilot CLI has no flag that makes its path  check follow links, and a prompt line enforces nothing). The README states the limit: in a review,  Copilot's `view` tool can open a file through a folder link or junction in the repo.- Docs: the README bullet of #110 ("not a file behind a folder link") now says a folder link is  shown once as a skipped entry, with no name or text behind it, and its Git Status lines are left  out; it also states the two limits (Copilot's `view` tool, and git still walking a junction). It  is a deliberate difference from upstream, for safety: Codex reads such files. On Windows the Git  Status lines behind a link are dropped; elsewhere git never lists them. A tracked file reached  through a junction keeps its name and diff, as today. The `git.mjs` header comment says the  same. The CHANGELOG entry names the walk limit. **Alternatives**: - Run Git Status with `":(exclude,literal)<link>"` pathspecs, so git does not walk the link for that  call: needs a second call for the tracked lines, and some thousand links would pass Windows'  command-line limit, a new way for a review to fail.- Rebuild the `??` lines of Git Status from the filtered list: one source of truth, but it copies  git's quoting rules for names with `"`, `\` and control characters.- Drop the via-link paths with no entry for the link: less output, but the review would not show  that a link was skipped, and macOS and Linux already show it. **Files likely to change**: - `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/git.mjs` (the filter, Git Status, the header comment)- `tests/git.test.mjs`, `tests/runtime-review-safety.test.mjs`- `README.md`, `plugins/copilot/CHANGELOG.md`, and the version files (`npm run bump-version -- 1.0.25`) **Tests to add or update**: the tests that make a junction on Windows use a folder symlinkelsewhere, as the existing tests do. Git on macOS and Linux lists a folder symlink as one entry, sothe tests marked "fails on Windows" pass there today and guard the result; only the Windows CI jobshows the fix. - `tests/git.test.mjs`, the existing test "an untracked file behind a folder link or junction ...":  its `win32` branch, which expects `### linkdir/key.txt (skipped: symlink)` and reads  `innerlink/ok.txt`, is removed. One set of checks then holds on every system: one `### linkdir  (skipped: symlink)` (and the same for `sub/linkdir`, `siblink`, `gitlink`, `innerlink`), and no  `linkdir/key.txt`, `gitlink/config` or `innerlink/ok.txt` anywhere in the output, also in Git  Status (fails on Windows today).- A junction or folder link to a git-ignored folder in the repo: neither its files' names nor their  text appear; the link is shown as skipped (fails on Windows today).- `getWorkingTreeState` on one repo: a link with two files and a subfolder behind it gives one entry;  a link nested in a folder behind another link gives only the top link; a link named with a space  (git quotes its `??` lines) and one with a non-ASCII letter give one entry each and no Git Status  line behind them; a plain untracked file and an untracked folder's files stay; the summary counts  each link once (fails on Windows today).- `dropLinkedStatusLines` on a status text with ` M app.js`, `?? linkdir/old.txt`,  `?? linkdir/new.txt` (a file `ls-files` never listed), `?? "link dir/a b.txt"`, `?? linkdir2.txt`  and `?? other/x.txt`, with the link folders `linkdir` and `link dir`: only ` M app.js`,  `?? linkdir2.txt` and `?? other/x.txt` stay (a prefix needs the `/`).- `unquoteGitPath`: `"a\tb"` gives `a<tab>b`, `"caf\303\251"` gives `café`, `"a\qb"` (an unknown  escape) gives `aqb`, `"linkdir/x` (no closing quote) gives `linkdir/x`, and `"linkdir/\377x"`  (a byte that is not UTF-8) gives `linkdir/` then U+FFFD and `x`. Through `dropLinkedStatusLines`,  the last two lines and `?? "linkdir/\qy"` are dropped under the link folder `linkdir`, and  `?? "other/\qy"` stays.- A nested repo: `nested/` stays as it is; a junction to a nested repo, listed as `linkdir/`, becomes  `linkdir` (the nested repo case is a guard; the junction case fails on Windows today).- `fs.lstatSync` mocked to throw for one folder on an untracked path, the second folder of  `outer/inner/secret.txt` (matched by its whole resolved path, built from the real repo root,  `fs.realpathSync.native(root)`, as the `mockRealpath` tests in `tests/git.test.mjs` do; every  other path goes to the real function; the test also checks that the mock was called, and calls  `getWorkingTreeState` and `collectReviewContext` with that real root): the entry collapses to  `outer/inner`, shown as `(skipped: broken symlink or unreadable file)`  (its own `formatUntrackedFile` call meets the same throw), and no name or text behind it appears  in the state, in Git Status, in either context mode, or in `untracked.md`; other files stay (fails  on the current code on every system). Skipped on Windows, a second case puts files named with a  tab and with `"` in that folder: their quoted `??` lines are gone too. Windows cannot make such  names, so a quoted name behind a real junction is guarded only by this mock and the  `dropLinkedStatusLines` test.- `unquoteGitPath`, on every system with the names it allows (a space and a non-ASCII  letter everywhere; a tab, a newline, `"`, `\`, U+0001 and U+007F on macOS and Linux): for each  untracked file, the name read back from its `??` line in `git status --short  --untracked-files=all` equals its name in `git ls-files -z --others` (a guard of the function  against git itself).- `fs.lstatSync` counted, for that folder's path only (every call goes to the real function),  over one `getWorkingTreeState` call, for a plain folder with three untracked files behind it: it  is checked once.- The stop-review-gate builds its context with `collectReviewContext` too  (`stop-review-gate-hook.mjs`), so these tests cover it.- The tests that check the filtered list also check `state.linkFolders`; the existing tests  compare only `state.untracked` and the context, so the new field does not change them.- The self-collect context (`includeDiff: false`) and `writeReviewPatches`' `untracked.md`: no name  through a link (fails on Windows today).- A tracked, changed file next to a link still shows in Git Status, as the first line with its  leading space (a guard; passes today).- Windows only: commit `tracked/file.txt`, then replace the folder `tracked` with a junction to a  copy in which `file.txt` is changed and `new.txt` is added (checked on 2026-10-28: git then shows  ` M tracked/file.txt` and `?? tracked/new.txt`). After the fix, Git Status keeps  ` M tracked/file.txt` and its diff, has no `tracked/new.txt` line, and the Untracked Files section  shows `### tracked (skipped: symlink)` (fails on Windows today).- `tests/runtime-review-safety.test.mjs`: its `win32` branch is removed; the review test with a  junction expects `### linkdir (skipped: symlink)` on every system, and the prompt Copilot gets  holds no `linkdir/key.txt` (fails on Windows today). **Checks**: `npm ci --include=dev`, `npm run build`, `npm test`, `npm run check-version`,`claude plugin validate .`; CI on all three systems; the release run after the merge. ## Risks & Considerations - `git ls-files --others` and `git status` still walk into a junction, so a junction to a big folder  can be slow. Git has no option to skip it.- Copilot's `view` tool can still open a file through a link in the repo, and quote it in its  answer. The probe ran on Windows with a junction; the README states it as seen there, and that a  folder symlink elsewhere is likely the same. The stop-review-gate needs no test of its own: it  builds its context with `collectReviewContext`.- Out of scope, and older than this change: Copilot's `view` tool opens `.git/config` directly, with  no link (the second probe), so a token in a remote URL can reach Copilot's answer and the job file.  That breaks Principle IV's job-file rule on main already; ticket #153 covers it.- A tracked or changed file reached through a junction stays in the diffs and Git Status, as today.  Git cannot track a path through a symlink; through a junction on Windows it is rare.- The untracked count in the summary counts the link once. ## Open Questions - None. ## Constitution Check - **I. Upstream parity**: met. Function names and layout stay; the filter and the README limit are  differences, recorded in the README section "Differences from the Codex plugin" and the `git.mjs`  header.- **II. Only reviewed code**: met. Node's `fs.lstatSync`; no new dependency.- **III. Copilot CLI through documented interfaces only**: met. No change to how Copilot is called;  the tool limit is documented, not worked around.- **IV. Safe by default**: met for this change. Reviews stay read-only (no change to the tool  profile), and the content the plugin builds (the prompt, the untracked list and the patch files)  now holds no name or text behind a link. This plan adds no way for a credential to reach a job  file and removes one. What Copilot's own `view` tool reads is not part of this plan: on main it  already reads files in the repo with or without a link, `.git/config` too, and can quote them in  its answer. That older gap against the job-file rule is #153's scope. #149's third acceptance  criterion lets this plan state the link case in the README instead.- **V. Cross-platform**: met. Junctions on Windows, folder symlinks elsewhere; CI runs all three.- **VI. Tested, including failure paths**: met. Links outside, into `.git`, to an ignored folder and  inside the repo, nested links, `nested/` entries, a folder that cannot be checked (also with  quoted names), the quoting against git, inline and self-collect, patch files, a tracked change  next to and under a link, and the summary count. No git call is  added. Patch release 1.0.25 with its `CHANGELOG.md` entry, then the release run on the merge  commit.

# Bug Fix: a review names the untracked files behind a folder link, and Copilot can read them - **Slug**: 149-skip-files-through-links- **Fixed**: 2026-10-28- **Assessment**: ./assessment.md- **Status**: applied ## Summary `getWorkingTreeState` now turns each untracked path that git reached through a folder link or ajunction into that link folder, once, so the untracked list, the file lists, the count and`untracked.md` show the link as skipped and nothing behind it. Git Status drops the `??` linesunder those folders. The README states the two limits the plugin cannot remove. ## Changes | File | Change | Notes ||------|--------|-------|| `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/git.mjs` | modified | `collapseLinkFolders` (a per-call `lstat` cache; a folder that cannot be checked counts as a link); `getWorkingTreeState` returns `linkFolders`; `unquoteGitPath` and `dropLinkedStatusLines`, exported; Git Status filtered; header comment || `tests/git.test.mjs` | modified, added tests | The existing link test has one set of checks on every system; new tests below || `tests/runtime-review-safety.test.mjs` | modified | The junction review test expects `### linkdir (skipped: symlink)` on every system and no `linkdir/key.txt` || `README.md` | modified | A "Differences from the Codex plugin" bullet with the two limits || `plugins/copilot/CHANGELOG.md` | modified | `### 1.0.25` entry || `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `plugins/copilot/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` | modified | `npm run bump-version -- 1.0.25` | ## Diff Highlights (optional) ```jsfor (const file of listed) {  const parts = file.split("/").slice(0, -1);  const link = parts.map((_, index) => parts.slice(0, index + 1).join("/")).find(isLinkFolder);  if (!link) {    untracked.push(file);  } else if (!linkFolders.includes(link)) {    linkFolders.push(link);    untracked.push(link);  }}``` ## Tests Added or Updated Git on macOS and Linux lists a folder symlink as one entry, so the tests marked "Windows" fail onmain only on Windows and guard the result elsewhere. All were run on main's `git.mjs` (with stubexports for the two new helpers) on Windows, where the listed ones failed. These fail on the old code: - "an untracked file behind a folder link or junction that leads outside the repo or into .git is  not read" (updated; Windows): one `### <link> (skipped: symlink)` for each of `linkdir`,  `sub/linkdir`, `siblink`, `gitlink`, `innerlink`; no `### <link>/` header or `?? <link>/` line,  and the names `linkdir/key.txt`, `siblink/key.txt`, `gitlink/config` and `innerlink/ok.txt`  nowhere in the output, also not in the self-collect Changed Files list.- "a junction or folder link to a git-ignored folder in the repo leaks no name or text" (Windows).- "each untracked path behind a link becomes the link once, with no Git Status line behind it"  (Windows): links with three files and a subfolder, a link in a folder behind a link, links  named with a space and with `ï`; ` M app.js` stays the first Git Status line; the summary counts 6.- "a nested repo stays one entry, and a link to a nested repo becomes the link" (Windows).- "a folder that cannot be checked counts as a link, and no name or text behind it is shown" (every  system): `fs.lstatSync` throws for `outer/inner`, which shows as `(skipped: broken symlink or  unreadable file)`; on macOS and Linux also with a tab and a `"` in the names behind it.- "a folder on many untracked paths is checked once" (every system).- "forced status colours do not let a name behind a link into Git Status" (every system): with  `color.status=always` and `color.ui=always`, git put a colour code before `??`, and the filter  kept the line; the Git Status call now passes `-c color.status=false`.- "a tracked change under a junction stays in Git Status, and the untracked file beside it is gone"  (Windows only).- "a review sends Copilot no file behind a folder link or junction that leads outside the repo"  (updated, in `tests/runtime-review-safety.test.mjs`; Windows).- "unquoteGitPath reads git's escapes and never throws on a broken name" and "dropLinkedStatusLines  drops only the untracked lines under a link folder" (new functions). This one guards the read-back against git itself: - "unquoteGitPath reads back each untracked name that git status prints": a space and `é`  everywhere; a tab, a newline, `"`, `\`, U+0001 and U+007F on macOS and Linux. ## Local Verification - Commands run: `npm ci --include=dev` (0 vulnerabilities), `npm run build` (pass), `npm test`  (518 tests: 476 pass, 42 skipped, 0 fail), `npm run check-version` (1.0.25),  `claude plugin validate .` (pass), on Windows.- Manual checks: the reproduction script on main's code showed `?? linkdir/key.txt`,  `?? seclink/key.txt` and the ignored file's text (assessment, Report). ## Deviations from Assessment - 2026-10-28: the assessment was written by hand in the format of `/speckit-bug-assess`, without  running that skill.- 2026-10-28: the README keeps the #110 bullet as it is and adds a new bullet next to it for the  link folder, the Git Status lines and the two limits, instead of rewording the #110 bullet: the  #110 bullet is still true, and one bullet per difference is easier to read.- 2026-10-28, review round 1: the mocked-folder test builds its path from the root that  `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` prints, as `makeRepoWithUntrackedFile` does, not from  `fs.realpathSync.native(root)`: that is the root `collectReviewContext` passes on, so the mock  matches the path the code checks, and the test asserts the mock fired. The folder check builds  the parent path step by step and stops at the first link. A link made between the `ls-files` and  the `status` call is not dropped from Git Status for that review (its text stays guarded by  `formatUntrackedFile`); the next review collapses it.- 2026-10-28, review round 2: the Git Status call passes `-c color.status=false`, which the  assessment did not plan: a forced colour setting put a code before `??` and hid lines from the  filter (Codex). Colour in the diffs is #61's scope. ## Follow-ups - #153: Copilot's `view` tool reads `.git/config` with no link.

# Bug Verification: a review names the untracked files behind a folder link, and Copilot can read them - **Slug**: 149-skip-files-through-links- **Tested**: 2026-10-28- **Assessment**: ./assessment.md- **Fix**: ./fix.md- **Result**: verified ## Summary The reproduction no longer shows the bug on Windows: a review of a repo with a junction to anoutside folder and a junction to a git-ignored folder names neither link's files and reads no textbehind them. The full suite passes with no regression; the checks ran again after review rounds 1 and 2.Copilot's `view` tool reaching through a link is not changed; it is the README limit the issueallows. ## Checks Performed | Check | Command / Action | Result | Notes ||-------|------------------|--------|-------|| Reproduction (pre-fix) | `collectReviewContext` on a repo with `linkdir` (a junction outside) and `seclink` (a junction to the ignored `secrets/`), main's `git.mjs` | fail (as expected) | `?? linkdir/key.txt`, `?? seclink/key.txt`, both `###` headers, and the ignored file's text || Reproduction (post-fix) | The same with this branch's `git.mjs` | pass | ` M app.js`, `### linkdir` and `### seclink` as skipped; no name or text behind them || New / updated tests | `node --test tests/git.test.mjs tests/runtime-review-safety.test.mjs` | pass | The tests listed in `fix.md` as failing on the old code failed on main's code on Windows and pass now || Regression suite | `npm test` | pass | 518 tests: 476 pass, 42 skipped, 0 fail || Lint / type-check | `npm run build` | pass | `tsc` type check || Version and plugin | `npm run check-version`, `claude plugin validate .` | pass | 1.0.25; validation passed | ## Output Excerpts ```textmain:         ?? linkdir/key.txt              ?? seclink/key.txt              ### seclink/key.txt              SECRET_IGNORED_MARKERthis branch:  M app.js              ### linkdir              ### seclink``` ## Residual Risks - Git still walks into a junction, so a junction to a big folder can make a review slow.- Copilot's `view` tool can open a file through a link in the repo (README limit); it can also open  `.git/config` with no link (#153).- The quoted-name cases behind a real junction cannot exist on Windows; the mocked-folder test and  the `dropLinkedStatusLines` test guard them. CI runs the macOS and Linux cases. ## Recommendation Close the bug: verified on Windows, where git walks into junctions; CI covers macOS and Linux.
